Question ID: MCR_U02_L05_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.AR.5

A savings account starts with $400 and grows by 5% each year. Which model represents the balance after t years?

feedback.text: This uses the percent as the factor. Growth keeps 100% and adds 5%, so the factor is 1.05.
Correct. The initial value is 400 and the 5% growth factor is 1.05.
This puts the initial value in the exponent position, which does not match the model.
This is linear addition, not exponential growth by a repeated factor.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U02_L05_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.AR.5

A car worth $18,000 loses 10% of its value each year. What is the decay factor?

feedback.text: This is the percent lost, not the amount remaining after the loss.
This would represent 10% growth, not decay.
Correct. After losing 10%, 90% remains, so the decay factor is 0.90.
This uses the percent as a whole number instead of a factor.
This applies 10% growth only once.
This adds 20% directly, but compounding multiplies by 1.10 twice.
This doubles the starting amount without using the growth factor.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U02_L05_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.AR.5

Which situation is best modeled exponentially?

answer.text: A plant doubles in height each week

feedback.text: Correct. Doubling each week means repeated multiplication.
This is a constant hourly rate, so it is linear.

answer.text: A taxi charges $5 plus $2 per mile

feedback.text: This has a constant additive change, so it is linear.

answer.text: A parking garage charges a flat fee

feedback.text: A flat fee does not show repeated multiplication.

Question ID: MCR_U02_L05_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.AR.5

In A = 750(0.92)ᵗ, what does 750 represent?

feedback.text: The decay factor is 0.92.
Correct. The initial value is the starting amount before any time passes.
The exponent t represents the number of time periods.
The percent decrease is related to 0.92, which means an 8% decrease.
